answer: I would anchor trust in Proof of unique courier route tenure with parcel carrier attestation. With routes the carrier recorded across years of rounds, a single forge check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the plume of that gap is the whole defence in one line. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the shale of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
